The Call to Action 19 health gaps, in one place

Source: R/trc.R
trchlthgap.Rd

For each health indicator of Call to Action 19 that the published tables measure, each group's estimate against non-Indigenous people's, with its interval, turned into one scale, the disadvantage ratio: the factor by which the group's outcome is worse (above

  1. or better (below 1).

Usage

trchlthgap(
  health = indiex("health"),
  lifeexp = indiex("lifeexp"),
  infmort = indiex("infantmort"),
  suiide = indiex("suicide"),
  ref = "Non-Indigenous"
)

Arguments

health

A health indicators table (default indiex("health"), table 13-10-0924), or NULL.

lifeexp

Life expectancy (default indiex("lifeexp"), table 17-10-0160), or NULL.

infmort

Infant mortality (default indiex("infmort"), table 17-10-0161), or NULL.

suiide

Suicidal thoughts (default indiex("suiide"), table 41-10-0021), or NULL.

ref

The reference group's label (default "Non-Indigenous").

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_trc_gaps: indicator, measure, period, group, estimate, refest, difference (group minus reference, on the indicator's scale), disratio, lower, upper, worse (the interval above 1), usewithcau. plot() draws it.

Details

The gaps come from indgap on the latest period of each table, with ref (non-Indigenous people) as the reference. To put years, rates and percentages on one scale, each gap is given as a ratio oriented by the indicator's better direction (trcind): the group's estimate over the reference's where lower is better (infant mortality, chronic conditions), the reference's over the group's where higher is better (life expectancy, good mental health, a regular provider): $$D = \hat\theta_g / \hat\theta_r \ \textrm{(lower is better)}, \qquad D = \hat\theta_r / \hat\theta_g \ \textrm{(higher is better)}.$$ It is a ratio of the published estimates, not a relative risk: for life expectancy, D = 1.1 means the reference lives 10% longer, not that the group's risk is 10% higher. Above 1 the group fares worse; the interval is the published one carried through (indgap's log-scale interval, inverted where needed). The difference on the indicator's own scale is kept beside it.

This is a description of gaps that Call 19 asks to be closed, measured as the surveys measure them; it is not a ranking of peoples. Report it with the trends (healchg) and the strengths (welprof) that sit beside it.

Each table is in the long layout of scests (or indiex()): columns group, indicator or measure, period, estimate, lower, upper, quality, and age for the health and suicidal-ideation tables (the all-ages total is used). The latest period with estimates is taken. Table 41-10-0021 publishes Indigenous groups only, so it adds a gap only when given a table with ref rows.

References

Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada (2015), see trcind.

See also

trcind, indgap.

Examples

g <- trchlthgap()
g[g$group == "Inuit", c("indicator", "measure", "period", "disratio",
                        "lower",
                        "upper")]
